A referendum on becoming a republic was held in South Africa on 5 October 1960. The Afrikaner -dominated right-wing National Party , which had come to power in 1948, was avowedly republican and regarded the position of Queen Elizabeth II as the South African monarch as a relic of British imperialism . [ 3 ] The National Party government subsequently organised the referendum on whether the then Union of South Africa should become a republic . The vote, which was restricted to whites —the first such national election in the union —was narrowly approved by 52.29% of the voters. [ 4 ] [ 5 ] The Republic of South Africa was constituted on 31 May 1961.
